rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who transgresses denies God's rights and rejects His blessing.
rows.anchor: جحد حقوق الله وكفر نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preferring worldly life means pursuing pleasures and following one's desires.
rows.anchor: آثر الحياة الدنيا اتباعا في طلب الشهوات ومتابعة المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is ignorant except the one who prefers God over self, spirit, this world, and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ما طلعت شمس ولا غربت على أحد إلا وهو جاهل، إلا من يؤثر الله تعالى على نفسه وروحه ودنياه وآخرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sign of disaffection from worldly life is that calamities become light, even the loss of one's child or self.
rows.anchor: قيل: ما علامة بغض الدنيا؟ قال: أن تهون عليه المصائب، حتى نفسه وولده

rows.speaker: مسلم بن يسار
rows.claim: When his son died, Muslim b. Yasar said grief for his son had distracted him from grieving over him, and asked God to make the reward he received through the loss belong to his son.
rows.anchor: كما قال مسلم بن يسار حين مات ولده: يا بني، شغلني الحزن لك عن الحزن عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sign is that even the pleasures of worldly life, including one's own life, become of little weight.
rows.anchor: والثاني يهون عليه نعيم الدنيا ولو روحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third sign is that nothing is nearer to the person than God.
rows.anchor: والثالث لا يكون شيء أقرب إليه من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: عامر بن عبد القيس
rows.claim: Amir ibn Abd al-Qays said that whenever he looked at anything, he saw God nearer to it than himself.
rows.anchor: كقول عامر بن عبد القيس: ما نظرت إلى شيء إلا رأيت الله أقرب إليه مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What deludes a person is what cuts him off from God despite God's gentleness and generosity.
rows.anchor: أي ما غرك بدونه فقطعك عنه مع لطفه وكرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing is nearer to the servant than the believer's heart; when something other than God enters it, that presence becomes a veil.
rows.anchor: وليس شيء أقرب إليه من قلب المؤمن، فإذا حضر الغير فيه فهو الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who beholds God with the heart becomes distant from everything besides Him.
rows.anchor: ومن نظر إلى الله بقلبه بعد عن كل شيء دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever seeks God's good pleasure, He makes content through His forbearance.
rows.anchor: ومن طلب مرضاته أرضاه بحلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When someone surrenders the heart to God, God takes charge of the limbs and makes them upright.
rows.anchor: ومن أسلم إلى الله تعالى قلبه تولى جوارحه فاستقامت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart's testimony reflects the degree to which a person has guarded the limbs.
rows.anchor: وإنما شهدت قلوبهم على قدر ما حفظوا من الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keep the heart steadfast in awareness that the Creator is with His creatures, and persist in works because God watches wherever people are.
rows.anchor: ألزموا قلوبكم، نحن مخلوقون وخالقنا معنا، ولا تملوا من أعمالكم، فإن الله شاهدكم حيثما كنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bring one's needs to God and remain at His door.
rows.anchor: وأنزلوا به حاجاتكم، وموتوا على بابه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognize one's ignorance, weakness, and incapacity while relying on God as the knower, strengthener, and able one.
rows.anchor: وقولوا: نحن جهال وعالمنا معنا، ونحن ضعفاء ومقوينا معنا، ونحن عاجزون وقادرنا معنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever remains in this reliance finds air, open space, earth, and sky all equal.
rows.anchor: فإن من لزمها كان الهواء والفضاء والأرض والسماء عنده سواء

rows.speaker: عمر بن واصل
rows.claim: Sahl's disciple Umar ibn Wasil said that ignorance in leaving God's protection was what deluded him when he recited the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن واصل تلميذ سهل: إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال: غرني الجهل بترك العصمة منك

words: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًۭا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person strives toward the Lord through deeds and encounters Him in connection with that striving.
rows.anchor: أي ساع بعملك إلى ربك سعيا

words: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًۭا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examine whether one's striving suits the Garden and nearness to God, or the Fire and distance from Him.
rows.anchor: فانظر في سعيك يصلح للجنة ولقربه أم للنار وبعده

rows.speaker: كهمس
rows.claim: Kamhas said he wept for forty years after taking a piece from a neighbor's wall for his guest to wash his hand, after buying the guest grilled fish for one daniq.
rows.anchor: وقد قال عمارة ابن زادان: قال لي كهمس: يا أبا سلمة أذنبت ذنبا فأنا أبكي عليه منذ أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the heaven is described as returning rain repeatedly.
rows.anchor: قال: ظاهرها ذات الرجع بالمطر بعد المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the earth's cleaving is the emergence of vegetation.
rows.anchor: الأرض ذات الصدع } [12] بالنبات،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the heart returns in remorse after sin.
rows.anchor: وباطنها القلب يرجع بالندم بعد الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's fissuring inwardly comes through conformity in deeds and words.
rows.anchor: الأرض تنصدع من الموافقات بالأفعال والأقوال
